jordyn: Heads-up — bringing up new embed model 'drydock-1.0' in staging. Did a quick int8 conversion and I'm seeing a recall@5 drop on the QA holdout (~6% absolute). Anyone seen this pattern? cc @maya @liam

maya: Yikes. Is that per-channel or per-tensor quant? Also what clipping percentile did you use?

jordyn: Per-channel symmetric, clip at 0.9999 percentile. Baseline fp16 recall@5 = 0.842, int8 = 0.779. Silhouette score down ~0.03. Ran a quick UMAP — topology looks like a couple of clusters merged (short queries).

liam: Can you paste the eval command and holdout size?

jordyn: 
```
# quick eval snippet
python eval/recall.py --model drydock-1.0-int8 --holdout ./data/holdout_10k.csv --k 5 --metric recall@
```
Holdout is 10k queries (mix of short/long). run id: r-20240312-drydock-int8-01

anya: Did you try bias correction or asymmetric per-channel? Sometimes symmetric clamps kill tail distances. Also how many clusters for kmeans?

jordyn: kmeans k=250. I tried asymmetric per-channel earlier (small improvement +1.2%), but still ~3.5% below fp16.

ryan: Try two things overnight: 1) per-layer scale sweep (layerwise clipping) 2) dynamic range computed on a larger calibration set (not just 10k). Also try int6 if the runtime supports it. Use `scripts/quant_scan.py --sweep=layerwise,clip_sweep --calib=100k`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging: drydock-1.0-int8 build succeeded. smoke tests 22/24 passed (1 flaky). run link: https://ci.internal/r-20240312-drydock-int8-01

maya: If the recall gap persists, we should do a small canary with fallback to fp16 for low-confidence queries (distance delta threshold). Also log nearest-neighbor id-flips for the affected queries.

jordyn: Plan: run per-layer sweep overnight, collect recall@k (1/5/10), id-flip heatmap, and UMAP snapshots. If no recovery, try int6 asymmetric and re-evaluate. I'll add the results to the onboarding doc: https://go/repo/drydock-onboard (wip).

liam: I'll add a microbatch/kv-cache warmup script to ensure any runtime masking differences aren't producing artifacts — will trigger a small rerun once you have the sweep outputs. :thumbsup:

maya: Also add a quick cluster purity check (sample top-3 neighbors for ~200 random queries) — sometimes numeric noise shuffles short-query neighbors.

jordyn: Sounds good. I'll post the overnight sweep summary in this thread tomorrow morning. Thanks all.
